subject: Dedicated reservation options for Borealis — sizing & ramp profiles
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moretti <alex.moretti@borealis.ai>, Priya Singh <priya@borealis.ai>
Date: 2027-07-21T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated reservation options for Borealis — sizing & ramp profiles

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Based on the workload profile you shared (mixed chat inference with bursts to ~250 qps, average request size ~350 tokens, 99th p90 latency target ~800ms) I put together three reservation pathways we think map well to your launch + growth windows. Attached is a short proposal (proposal-dedicated-borealis-v1.pdf) and a working cost model (borealis-cost-model.xlsx).

High level options (summary):

- Starter (12 A100-80GB reserved) — for low-risk launch, covers baseline traffic with autoscale burst to 24; 12-month term recommended for pricing. Canary period: 4 weeks, can reduce to month-to-month after 90-day metrics review.
- Growth (24 A100-80GB reserved + 40 burst) — target for predictable active users and steady growth; includes dedicated KV cache warmers and prefetch slots to reduce cold-start token cost. Suggested ramp: 25% capacity month 1, 60% month 2, 100% month 3.
- Enterprise (48 mixed H100/A100 pool with regional redundancy) — for aggressive scale, SLA-backed latencies and multi-region failover.

Notes/assumptions:
- We recommend reserving at least 25% of baseline capacity as committed (min GPUs) to keep latency SLOs under burst.
- Quantized 8-bit model variants can typically reduce GPU needs by ~20-30% for your prompt mix; we can validate on a short perf pass.
- Autoscaling policies: we suggest continuous batching for steady traffic and aggressive prewarm for known campaign windows.

Next steps I suggest: you tell us which pathway aligns to your budget/risk profile and we’ll return a detailed ramp schedule, expected p50/p95 token cost, and procurement PO template.

Attachments: proposal-dedicated-borealis-v1.pdf, borealis-cost-model.xlsx, kube-reference.yaml

Best,
Hannah Schmitt

Alex / team — quick sizing notes from infra + perf:

- Context: your 4k context and mixed-length replies push per-token cost up; we benchmarked a similarly-provisioned 70B-class model on A100-80GB with continuous batching and KV-cache enabled. Observed numbers: a single A100-80GB sustained (production-tuned kernel set) can comfortably sustain ~7–12 qps for the prompt shape you described when aiming for p95 < 1s at 4k context. Numbers vary by model variant and batching profile.

- Recommendation: for Growth plan with 350 qps short spikes, we recommend a committed baseline of 18–20 A100-80GB (this gets you through sustained daytime traffic with room for autoscale), with capacity to burst to ~44 GPUs using reserved burst slots; that keeps p95 below target for the majority of spikes.

- Quantization: moving to an int8 pipeline typically reduces GPU requirement by ~25–30% depending on accuracy tradeoffs for your tasks. If you can accept a small regen check on worst-case prompts, baseline could drop to ~14–15 GPUs. We'll run a 48–72 hour perf verification on your representative prompt set.

- Peering / on-prem: we support VPC peering and direct connect. For VPC peering we need a /29 for control-plane endpoints and a short-lived tunnel for peering during onboarding. I attached a light architecture sketch (kube-reference.yaml) in the proposal for your network folks. For air-gapped on-prem installs, we'd need an additional compliance packet and longer lead times.

- Ramp schedule (suggested):
  * Week 0–4: Canary — 25% of Growth baseline (6 GPUs) with close telemetry
  * Month 1: 40% baseline (9 GPUs)
  * Month 2: 70% baseline (14 GPUs)
  * Month 3: 100% baseline (20 GPUs) and enable burst pool up to 44 for campaign windows

I'll share exact perf numbers from our internal runs once the perf pass completes. Happy to sync with your infra/security team if helpful.

—Marcus
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Updated: Dedicated reservation recommendation + ramp (Growth option)

Alex / Priya — thanks for the quick turnaround. Based on Marcus' sizing and your ramp targets, attached is an updated proposal (proposal-dedicated-borealis-v2.pdf) and an updated cost tab in the workbook. Summary of the recommended Growth path:

- Committed baseline: 20 A100-80GB reserved GPUs (12-month term)
- Burst pool: up to 24 additional reserved burst GPUs (total pool 44)
- Canary window: 4 weeks — start with 25% baseline and observe p95 / token cost
- Suggested ramp: Week0 25% -> Month1 40% -> Month2 70% -> Month3 100%
- Quantization option: run a 48hr perf pass on your prompt set; if acceptable we expect baseline to drop to ~14–15 GPUs (savings captured in the attached cost model).

Procurement & next steps:
1) Sign the attached SOW + PO terms and return — we’ll provision a dedicated pool and schedule the perf pass.
2) Security: share a contact for your security engineer and we’ll send the VPC peering checklist / SOC2 evidence pack.
3) Kickoff: once PO is in, we’ll schedule a 2-day onboarding (network, access, perf pass).

Attachments: proposal-dedicated-borealis-v2.pdf, borealis-cost-model.xlsx, kube-reference.yaml

Would you like a short call this week to walk through procurement items?

Best,
Hannah
